steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Perception is the process of interpreting sensory information to make sense of the world. Sensation is detecting stimuli; perception is interpreting them - they are distinct processes. | Key Fact: Gregory's constructivist theory: perception uses past experience and expectations to interpret sensory input (top-down processing). Visual illusions support this - we misinterpret because we apply assumptions (e.g. the Muller-Lyer illusion). | Key Fact: Gibson's direct theory: perception is entirely determined by sensory input from the environment (bottom-up processing). We perceive affordances - what the environment offers us (e.g. a chair affords sitting). No past experience needed. | Key Fact: Factors affecting perception: culture (Hudson's study showed Western and non-Western people

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Compare Gregory's constructivist theory with Gibson's direct theory of perception. | Explain how culture can affect perception, using research evidence. | Evaluate what visual illusions tell us about the nature of perception.
